proposed_widenings.name: on_feature_trigger class-feature mechanics family
proposed_widenings.justification: Sear Undead is not independently activated — it fires automatically whenever Turn Undead is used. No existing ClassFeatureMechanics family represents a passive save-gate rider on another feature's resolution. The only family is 'activation', which requires UseCountResource and RestResetCadence, but Sear Undead has no independent resource pool or reset cadence — it fires unlimited times, once per Turn Undead use.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8)

proposed_widenings.name: ability_modifier variant of LevelAxis
proposed_widenings.justification: The die count scales with the caster's Wisdom modifier, not any level axis. LevelAxis currently covers character, class, slot, subclass, proficiency_bonus — none of which model ability-score-derived scaling. A new axis variant (e.g., ability_modifier with an Ability field, or a dedicated wis_modifier axis) is needed to express 'WisMod d8s'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8)

proposed_widenings.name: damage variant of ClassFeatureEffect
proposed_widenings.justification: ClassFeatureEffect = GrantExtraActionEffect | HealHpEffect. Sear Undead's payload is Radiant damage. A DamageEffect variant (matching the spell-surface DamageEffect shape: damageType + DiceAmount) is needed for class feature effects.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll's total.

notes: Three distinct gaps block honest encoding. Primary: no class-feature mechanics family exists for a passive augmentation rider on another feature's save gate (structural). Secondary: LevelAxis has no ability_modifier variant for Wis-mod scaling, and ClassFeatureEffect has no damage variant (both surface). All three would need to be added before an honest encoding is possible. The 'this damage doesn't end the turn effect' clause (damage is additive, not a substitute resolution) is a semantic note that a future surface design should accommodate as well.
